traits.shade_tolerance.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), Fraxinus latifolia, Reaction to Competition (p. 341): 'The species is classed as intermediate in tolerance of shade'.

traits.self_pruning.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), Fraxinus latifolia, Reaction to Competition (p. 341): 'Individuals self-prune quickly with side shade, and forest-grown trees have long, clean trunks'.

traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 28 Oregon ashes: 0.276 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 27 Oregon ashes 25 years or older (Longview, WA): 0.63. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 27 Oregon ashes 25 years or older (Longview, WA): 0.16 (quartiles 0.13 and 0.21). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.3, 0.28, 0.24], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, Fraxinus latifolia (read 2026-10-18): "a medium-sized deciduous tree".

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Fraxinus latifolia (read 2026-10-18): the leaves "turn bright yellow and fall off early in autumn". Colour ours.

traits.leaf_fall_months.note: Wikipedia, Fraxinus latifolia (read 2026-10-18): the leaves "fall off early in autumn": October, ahead of the October to November most broadleaves are given. Month ours.

traits.flowering_months.note: Seed Manual, Fraxinus chapter (printed p. 538): April and May, with no place given. Too few iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands are annotated as flowering to count (3).

traits.fruiting_months.note: Seed Manual, Fraxinus chapter (printed p. 538): ripe in August and September.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Fraxinus latifolia: grows 10 m to 25 m tall.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Ash, Oregon, green: modulus of elasticity 7,800 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.5).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Ash, Oregon, green: modulus of rupture 52,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Fraxinus latifolia (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.53 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.53, branches 0.56. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region. Refitted 2026-10-23 (11.5 to 16) when the reference became the Urban Tree Database's open-grown Oregon ashes, 23 m at 50 years, kept short enough that no grown plant passes Abrams's greatest height of 25 m.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Fraxinus, table 3, read): minimum seed-bearing age 30 years. No FEIS review was found. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 10 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a medium-sized tree with a narrow, rounded crown, opposite branching and pinnately compound leaves of five to seven broad leaflets. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: The USDA Urban Tree Database's open-grown Oregon ashes (Longview, WA): 11 trees 43 to 53 years old, median 23 m tall and 65 cm through, read as 50 years. Was 18 m and 40 cm at 50 years, from general knowledge (broadleaf revision 28).

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: light green leaves; grey-brown bark in interlacing diamond ridges. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: dense hanging clusters of single green samaras 3 to 5 cm long. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: small flowers before the leaves in March and April; samaras green in summer, tan from September, falling into the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): grey-brown bark deeply furrowed into interlacing ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaflets narrower than shade leaflets; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
